description: Solo team from Jeddah. I'm an Electrical and Computer Engineering student using NISAR radar data to track how center-pivot farms in northern Saudi Arabia change across a season.
summary: Echofield uses NASA-ISRO NISAR L-band radar to follow center-pivot farms in the Basaita area of Al Jouf, Saudi Arabia, through nine acquisitions from June to October 2026. Measured against empty desert, the radar shows 33 regions where the HV signal increased and 19 where it decreased, and active vegetated area rising from 19.4 to 29.1 km². I checked the radar against optical NDVI from NASA HLS: in 37 of 38 fields the two rise and fall together (median ρ = 0.72), and when radar calls a field active, optical agrees 90% of the time. The website lets anyone step through the season and explore each field’s radar and optical record.
details:
Al Jouf’s center-pivot farms draw on groundwater that does not refill, so knowing which fields are active, and when, matters for water and food security. I read only a 20 km window from each NISAR GCOV file in the cloud (track 71, frame 17, ascending, 20 m pixels, HH and HV), reduced speckle, converted to decibels and measured every date against the same patch of empty desert. The desert noise was 0.50 dB, so only changes above 1.5 dB were counted.

Change regions: 33 regions where HV increased and 19 where it decreased between June 19 and October 17. These are connected groups of changed pixels, not verified field boundaries. In one example field, HV peaked on July 25 and fell 5.9 dB by August 18. Optical NDVI fell from 0.53 to 0.29 in the same window, so two independent sensors show the same decline, most likely a harvest.

Active area: pixels more than 4 dB above desert grew from 19.4 km² to 29.1 km², and the rise held at 3 and 5 dB.

Field detection: a Hough circle transform proposed 55 circles, and 38 passed my visual inspection (a candidate acceptance rate of 69%). In a 6 km sample box the detector found 8 of about 18 fields, an approximate recall of 44%.

Optical validation: NDVI from NASA HLS, with every radar date matched to a clear scene 0 to 1 day apart. Pooled over 342 field-date pairs, Spearman ρ = 0.50; per field, 37 of 38 are positive (median 0.72). Active/inactive agreement at 4 dB is 58% (kappa 0.25). Almost all disagreement is green fields below the radar threshold, consistent with L-band’s weakness for short or young crops. The site reports agreement at other thresholds without changing the one I chose.

Limits: radar cannot name the crop. HH and HV both respond to moisture, roughness and vegetation, so the HH rise about 7 weeks before the HV peak is only a possible moisture or surface change. The products are provisional, the August 6 pass is missing, and the window is outside the main winter wheat season.

Built with Python in Google Colab (earthaccess, h5py, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-image, rasterio, Matplotlib) and a single HTML/CSS/JavaScript page on GitHub Pages. The code is open source under the MIT license.
